title: Decoction, infusion and hydroalcoholic extract of Origanum vulgare L.: different performances regarding bioactivity and phenolic compounds
summary: Compared the three preparations for antioxidant and antibacterial activity and phenolic compounds. The abstract reports activity against Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria; the hydroalcoholic extract showed the strongest activity against E. coli.
comparison: Includes an infusion, the same preparation type recorded in the Sharr study; equivalence of plant material and method is unconfirmed.
limitation: Laboratory assays, not a human treatment study. The study preparation and plant material are not established as identical to the Sharr Mountains record.

title: Pharmacological evaluation of aqueous extract of Althaea officinalis flower grown in Lebanon
summary: Tested an aqueous flower extract in rat models of inflammation, gastric ulcer and blood lipids, and in an in-vitro platelet aggregation assay. The authors reported anti-inflammatory and antiulcer activity in the tested models.
comparison: Related water-based preparation, but not an exact match: the Sharr study records a flower infusion; this paper tested a prepared aqueous extract.
limitation: Animal and laboratory research, not evidence of benefit in people. It used a prepared aqueous extract, not necessarily the same flower infusion or dose recorded in the Sharr Mountains study.

title: Chemical characterization and in vitro biological evaluation of aqueous extract of Althaea officinalis L. flower grown in Lebanon
summary: Characterized a water extract of marshmallow flowers and tested antioxidant, inflammatory-response, red-blood-cell protection and cell-growth outcomes in laboratory assays.
comparison: Close plant-part and solvent match: the paper notes the flowers are consumed as hot infusions, but its laboratory extract used a 3-hour room-temperature maceration followed by warming to 60 °C, so it is not the same preparation method.
limitation: In-vitro assays only; the cell-growth findings do not demonstrate treatment of cancer or other disease in people. The preparation method and plant material differ from the Sharr record.

title: Infusion and decoction of wild German chamomile: bioactivity and characterization of organic acids and phenolic compounds
summary: Compared chamomile infusion and decoction with a methanol extract. All samples showed antioxidant activity; infusion and methanol extract inhibited growth in two human cancer cell lines in vitro, while decoction did not show that activity.
comparison: Includes an infusion, matching the preparation type in the Sharr record. The tested material and infusion method are not confirmed to be the same.
limitation: Cell-culture findings do not show cancer treatment benefit in people. This study tests lab outcomes and does not establish that the Sharr Mountains preparation has the same composition or effects.
